title: Federal Reserve Board announces final individual capital requirements for large banks, effective on October 1
summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced final individual capital requirements for large banks on August 29, 2025, effective October 1, 2025. The requirements are based on stress test results and include a 4.5% minimum CET1 requirement, at least 2.5% stress capital buffer, and applicable capital surcharges for the largest banks. Morgan Stanley's requirement is pending as the firm requested reconsideration to reduce its stress capital buffer.
key_points: Federal Reserve finalized individual capital requirements for large banks, effective October 1, 2025
Minimum CET1 capital requirement is 4.5% for all banks subject to the requirements
Stress capital buffer requirement is at least 2.5% based on stress test results
Capital surcharges for largest/most complex banks are updated annually in Q1 to reflect systemic risk
Board proposed averaging stress test results over two consecutive years to reduce year-over-year volatility
Morgan Stanley's stress capital buffer requirement is pending reconsideration, with final decision expected by September 30, 2025
why_it_matters: These capital requirements directly affect how much capital large banks must hold against potential losses, influencing their ability to lend and distribute capital. Banks below their total requirement face automatic restrictions on capital distributions and discretionary bonus payments. The proposed averaging of stress test results over two years would reduce volatility in capital requirements, providing more predictability for bank capital planning.
market_structure_context: The announcement relates to bank regulatory capital framework (CCAR stress testing and capital requirements). Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman noted this represents a period of transition, with the Board committed to reducing year-over-year volatility and increasing transparency of the stress test.
